newsitem.title: UK: Gunmen torch train in N.Ireland protest.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen torch train in N.Ireland protest.

text.p: Masked gunmen boarded a train at Newry station, 40 miles (70 km) south of Belfast on Tuesday afternoon and set it ablaze, police said.
They could not confirm reports that the gang told passengers they were members of the underground Irish Republican Army, which is fighting British rule of Northern Ireland.
Police said the men left behind plastic bags which were assumed to contain incendiary material and the train caught fire. Passengers were on the train at the time but managed to escape.
The train was thought to be operated by Ireland's state CIE railway company which operates trains between the Irish capital, Dublin and Belfast.
It was the latest act of violence since protests erupted over the routing of a Protestant Orange Order parade through a Catholic part of Portadown on Sunday.
